chapter: Scrapbook: Sharkey Bonano years at the Famous Door
title: Sunday concerts, Bourbon Street Bounce and Curly Lima
summary: Allen recalls the 1949 Sunday concerts and Harvey Blackstone's Bourbon Street Bounce; Riddick remembers writer and bartender Curly Lima.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You know, I should remember this. Every Saturday morning we played on there. I should remember these Sunday concerts. It says, opening today, Sunday, September 4th, 1949. It's just about the time I came here. It was in the American Legion Crystal Room. 334. Well, that was on Royal Street, yes. But I really don't remember that. Back to corner of Conta. That may have been just before I got here.
Tom, uh, uh, uh, uh, Tommy Griffin. Tom Griffin.
I talked to, uh, Harvey Blackstone, who wrote Bourbon Street Bounce yesterday. Do you remember Bourbon Street Bounce?
I don't know whether I do or not. I can play it in five minutes if, if, uh, if somebody would start it off.
Well, you probably even recorded. Oh, I know I played it many a time. Yeah.
Bourbon Street Parade and Bourbon Street Bounce.
Well, Harvey's over in Tyler now. That's what reminded me of it when you mentioned Tyler, Texas.
Let's hear it again. Curly Lima. Oh, I remember him. Oh, yeah. Curly used to do a lot of writing things for picking of the item. He worked as a bartender. Yes. Curly died of cancer.
